The local basis changes at the two ends of a qutrit maximally entangled with a qubit: SU(3) at
one end, SU(2) at the other, and a relative phase that neither end owns.

Embedded, so far without confirmation

Read instead as one pair

SU(5) (Georgi and Glashow, 1974), then SO(10), E₆ and
supersymmetric versions. No proton decay has been seen,
and no superpartner has appeared.

The group is familiar as the stabilizer of a 3 + 2 split in

symmetry of one entangled pair.

C LU E 3 · A N U L L R E S U LT

No substructure: undetectable, or undistillable?
Every particle behaves as a point

Bound entanglement

Searches for the excited states and contact interactions
that constituents would produce have returned nothing.
Yet three generations repeating one set of charges is the
kind of pattern that has always signaled constituents,
from the periodic table to the hadrons.

Certifiably entangled, yet no local operations and classical
communication distill a maximally entangled pair from
any number of copies (Horodecki, Horodecki and
Horodecki, 1998). It first becomes possible when d₁d₂ >
6, and a witness can detect it.

On this reading, the substructure of elementary matter would not be
undetectable. It would be undistillable.

Chain Theory studies finite networks of maximally entangled pairs of qudits, joined at shared qudits
with no fixed identification of bases across the joins, and known only through what distillation can fix

D I S T I L L AT I O N

To distill two qudits is to project them onto the maximally entangled state of their common support: a generalized
distillation, with one copy, one joint projection, and no failure branch. Between pairs it moves entanglement without
adding any, and a single read fails to fix the ends of a pair exactly where standard distillation fails to reach every
entangled state, at d₁d₂ > 6.

THE AXIOM

Nothing exists but finitely many maximally
entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared,
known only by distilling them.
The only input. In the spirit of Wheeler’s “it from bit” (1989), with finite quantum systems in place
of bits.

THE AXIOM

Five definitions of the axiom’s terms
Word

Definition

qudit

a finite-dimensional quantum system, of dimension at least two, since a one-dimensional system ends no pair

shared

a qudit that is an end of two or more pairs, carried as one copy per pair; the copies are one qudit, so exchanging
two pairs moves only their far ends

distill

project two qudits of dimensions d₁, d₂ onto P_m = |ω_m⟩⟨ω_m| on their common support, m = min(d₁, d₂); the
output is the pair of their type

read

an act at one end of a pair that distills the two ends in a basis of that end, one read for each of its d + 1 mutually
unbiased bases, and passes the basis along the pair, leaving the far end in ⟨e|ω_m⟩ at each element |e⟩, since (A
⊗ 1)|ω⟩ = (1 ⊗ Aᵀ)|ω⟩; the basis reaches the far end whole, so a read is taken at the larger end

known

what its reads fix jointly, under every matching of its pairs and every exchange of its reads or pairs; two
anticommuting reads also fix their product, whose sign flips with their order

A pair, or link, of type (d₁, d₂) joins two qudits in the maximally entangled state on their common support, |ω_m⟩ = (1/√m) Σᵢ |i⟩|i⟩. A
matching, a change of basis by a unitary U of the support, acts on the pair as U ⊗ Ū and leaves it unchanged. To fix is to determine
with certainty from a single copy, not to estimate an expectation value over many. Certainty leaves nothing open, which gives the
read cap.
The definitions spell out the axiom’s terms; their properties follow from it (the Letter’s Supplemental Material, Sec. S1).

Chain Theory · The axiom

The readout of a configuration, a set of links some of them read. R holds the
whole operator space of each read link and the traceless part of each unread
link. The bare insertion, the identity of R, reads one; the dressed insertion M
weighs only what the reads fix.

THE DEFINITION OF FIX

Readable or dark: readable exactly when d₁d₂ ≤ 6
C E R TA I N T Y L E AV E S N O T H I N G O P E N

A read fixes two ends only when every consistent
relation between them, every positive map
between their operator algebras, is of a kind
distillations carry.
Reads compose only decomposable maps, so a type is readable
when every positive map between its ends is decomposable,
and dark otherwise. No state is bound entangled: what no
distillation carries is a relation, not a state.

THE SIX GENRES

Six genres of link, two of
them readable
A link’s genre is the pair of its end dimensions, written larger end
first. Under the read cap, (2,2) and (3,2) are readable; the other
four are dark.
The upper part of each cell is derived. The amber band is
conjectured: the sector of physics each genre is taken to
correspond to.
That ends have dimension two, three or four is the compendium’s box
1.7, “Conjecture 0”, graded a conditional theorem under its move
table. A one-dimensional end is excluded at the axiom (theorem 2.9).

O N E E X AC T N U M B E R

The sharpest test is a number
Measured, not derived
α(0) is known to about one part in ten billion, one of the most precisely
measured numbers in science, yet the Standard Model takes it from
experiment.

Hard to hit by accident
Its digits show no pattern. A simple value like the 2/3 of Koide’s lepton-mass
relation can be reached by many short formulas. Ten digits of 137.035 999…
cannot.

Nothing left to tune
Proposed closed forms foundered on their normalization: a volume can be
rescaled, and the number with it (Wyler 1969, 1971; Robertson 1971; Gilmore
1972). A derivation must leave nothing to fix.

O N E E X AC T N U M B E R

The central charge picks one readable genre
The identification algebra of a link, su(d₁) ⊕ su(d₂) ⊕ u(1),
is the infinitesimal basis changes at its two ends. Its center
is spanned by

Q = i diag(d₂ 1, −d₁ 1)
which acts on the whole link, its pair ket included, as the
scalar i(d₂ − d₁): zero at (2,2), and i at (3,2).

At (3,2)
The algebra is su(3) ⊕ su(2) ⊕ u(1), of S(U(3) × U(2)) ≅
(SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1))/ℤ₆
Q = 6iY, with Y = diag(½, ½; −⅓, −⅓, −⅓) the hypercharge
generator
The link carries (3,2) with Y = 1/6, the quantum numbers
of the left-handed quark doublet
The pair’s stabilizer has dimension four, its center U = i
diag(1, 1; −1, −1, 0)

So exactly one readable genre carries an acting central charge. Its charge is the hypercharge direction; the passage to electric
charge lies beyond the Letter.

Weigh each record
Every antisymmetric record weighs 1. A symmetric record weighs √3
on a solid edge and √2 on a dashed edge, as marked; each commutator
weighs √6.
Why: a symmetric record survives the mirror, and its letter then runs
over the d matched directions of a pair at amplitude 1/√d each, giving d
· 1/√d = √d. On solid edges the mirror is the Letter’s exchange of reads,
at the qutrit (d = 3); on dashed edges, its exchange of links, which
moves the qubits (d = 2). Commutators survive both.
Note the bottom edge: its letters sit at the qubits, yet it takes √3,
because a read is an act at the end where it is taken, the qutrit.

W AY 2 · BY SY M M E T RY · S T E P 1 O F 2

Symmetric and
antisymmetric squares
Take n directions e₁, …, eₙ, a basis of a space V. Ordered pairs eᵢeⱼ, one
direction in each place, number n² and span V ⊗ V. Swapping the two
places sorts them into two kinds.
Sym²n: the symmetric combinations, eᵢeᵢ and eᵢeⱼ + eⱼeᵢ for i < j.
There are n(n + 1)/2.
Λ²n: the antisymmetric combinations, eᵢeⱼ − eⱼeᵢ for i < j. There are
n(n − 1)/2.

Here Sym²n and Λ²n name these counts: Sym²8 = 36, Λ²8 = 28, Sym²3
= 6, Λ²3 = 3. Two different sets of m and n directions, swapped into
each other, give m · n of each kind.

2. Reads at the qutrit fix the qubit, and reads at the qubit do not fix the qutrit: the end rule.
3. Every one of the link’s records is an eigenvector of the exchange of the two reads.
